text: Why is Kerr-based all-optical logic impractical in silicon at telecom wavelengths?
choices: Silicon is opaque at 1550 nm, so no light propagates through the waveguide
The Kerr coefficient (n2) of silicon is exactly zero
Two-photon absorption removes the light before the Kerr phase shift can build up; silicon's nonlinear FOM (~7.7e-7) is about six orders of magnitude below the ~0.08 threshold
Silicon's thermo-optic coefficient exactly cancels the Kerr effect at room temperature
explanation: At the fluences needed for Kerr bistability, silicon's large two-photon absorption absorbs the photons first, and its figure of merit n2/(lambda*beta_TPA) is about 7.7e-7, roughly six orders of magnitude below the ~0.08 needed. Silicon is transparent (not opaque) at 1550 nm and has a nonzero Kerr coefficient, so the barrier is TPA, not opacity, a null nonlinearity, or thermo-optics.
